subject: Sampling speed on mac vs ubuntu

messages.author: b17f4d0880547804
messages.subject: Sampling speed on mac vs ubuntu
parts:
Hi all,
I've built a fairly complex hierarchical model (600 + parameters) parameterised from N = 180,000 +.
I'm not having issues with getting the model to converge and I've implemented all the tricks to speed it up.
On my iMac it takes about 60 hours to complete 4000 iterations (iMac: 4 GHz Intel Core i7, 16 GB RAM).

What I have found odd though is when I put this model onto a AWS EC2 optimised compute instance (e.g. c4.2xlarge; https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/instance-types/) using linux docker containers the model takes over 200 hours to complete. This is despite using the same initials.
Sure the processor on my iMac is slightly faster then what is available on c4.2xlarge (3.5 GHz) but the difference in processor speed doesn't look like it explains this much of a difference.
I know there are differences in how the models are compiled and sampled between different operating systems could this be the discrepancy in wall time?

Cheers
J

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Sampling speed on mac vs ubuntu
parts:
Hi, maybe 4000 iterations is more than you need?  This does sound like it could be a good example for the “cavity search” algorithm.
A
